last.minutes: We are executing a minor rebalancing of our spot book to bring AAVE and BTC back under the strict 30% single-coin concentration limit, while keeping our core allocations in high-conviction assets like SOL and PEPE. In the futures book, we maintain our 2x short on NEAR, as the fundamental catalyst of the protocol exploit remains a strong headwind despite short-term price volatility. We decline the aggressive risk team's suggestion to increase leverage to 3x to avoid premature stop-outs in a neutral market regime.
notes: scaled the spot book from 98% to 95% invested

futures.why: Capitalizing on fundamental weakness and negative sentiment following the major protocol exploit.

spot.why: Strong quant trend strategy performance and solid fundamentals support holding AAVE within compliance limits.

lessons.text: Promptly cutting underperforming positions frees up capital for high-conviction leaders while minimizing losses from lagging assets.
Strictly adhering to portfolio concentration limits while minimizing unnecessary churn prevents compliance breaches and preserves capital from excessive transaction costs.
High transaction costs and the 31.2% tax on profitable sales mean that churning small positions is often more damaging than holding through minor volatility.
Strictly enforcing concentration limits and rotating out of overcrowded positions protects capital from unexpected liquidation risks.

Minimizing unnecessary adjustments to profitable spot positions helps avoid triggering the 31.2% tax and high transaction fees, while rebalancing should be reserved primarily for regulatory compliance.
